  Now I'll refactor `ParseDSMLToolCalls` to a strict internal version that tracks violations, keeping the exported signature:

  <｜｜DSML｜｜tool_calls>
  <｜｜DSML｜｜invoke name="write_file">
  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="end_line" string="false">301</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="path" string="true">internal/dsml/dsml.go</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="start_line" string="false">290</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="content" string="true">func ParseDSMLToolCalls(text string) ([]DSMLCall, error) {
  	calls, _, err := parseDSMLToolCallsStrict(text)
  	return calls, err
  }

  // dsmlToolCallsWrapperRe matches any tool_calls wrapper tag (open or close,
  // including the typo'd _calls cousins) anywhere in the text. A wrapper
  // presence test that is NOT anchored, unlike dsmlToolCallsCloseEndRe.
  var dsmlToolCallsWrapperRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)</?\s*(?:tool_calls|_calls)\s*>`)

  // parseDSMLToolCallsStrict extracts all DSML tool calls and, on the side,
  // reports whether the emission deviated from the strict format the prompt
  // demands (the violated flag feeds ParseDSMLMessage's OK=false). The bool is
  // a coarse summary - callers only need "strict or not", never the precise
  // violation list. Calls are still returned (and executed) when violations
  // exist; only a truncation (unclosed > 0) aborts with an error.
  func parseDSMLToolCallsStrict(text string) ([]DSMLCall, bool, error) {
  	original := text
  	text = normalizeDSMLText(text)
  	violated := text != original // violation #2: normalize repaired markup

  	// Truncation check by state-machine scan: named <invoke> opens are
  	// matched against </invoke> closes in text order, with <parameter>
  	// bodies treated as opaque content (a raw "<invoke" or "</invoke>"
  	// inside a parameter VALUE is content, not structure). A cut-off
  	// emission (an opening tag never closed) must never be executed.
  	// Unlike an opens-vs-closes count, a stray "</invoke>" in prose can
  	// never satisfy an unclosed call (false negative); unlike stripping
  	// complete blocks first, a nested or mis-nested open (two opens, one
  	// close) is still detected instead of being silently swallowed.
  	blocks, unclosed, _, strays, implicitClose := dsmlBlockRangesStrict(text)
  	if unclosed > 0 {
  		return nil, violated, fmt.Errorf("DSML tool call truncated: %d unclosed <invoke>", unclosed)
  	}
  	violated = violated || len(strays) > 0     // violation #3: stray invoke close
  	violated = violated || implicitClose        // violation #4: missing invoke close implicitly closed
  	violated = violated || IsDSMLToolCallCut(text) // violation #5: cut-off wrapper close
  	if dsmlToolCallsCloseEndRe.MatchString(strings.TrimSpace(text)) {
  		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
  		if strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "</_calls>") || strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "<_calls>") {
  			violated = true // violation #5: typo'd wrapper close
  		}
  	}
  	if !dsmlToolCallsWrapperRe.MatchString(text) {
  		violated = true // violation #5/#6: no tool_calls wrapper at all (bare invoke)
  	}
  	if len(blocks) == 0 {
  		return nil, violated, nil
  	}

  	var calls []DSMLCall
  	covered := -1 // closeEnd of the most recently parsed top-level block
  	for _, b := range blocks {
  		// A block directly nested inside another one (outside any
  		// <parameter> body - those are opaque to the scan) is a structural
  		// accident, not a second call: executing both would double-run the
  		// inner tool. Skip it here just like StripDSMLToolCalls does.
  		if b.openStart < covered {
  			continue
  		}
  		covered = b.closeEnd
  		body := text[b.openEnd:b.closeStart]
  		// Mask nested blocks inside this body so their <parameter> tags are
  		// invisible to the extraction regex: the enclosing call must not
  		// pick up arguments the model meant for the accidental inner call.
  		for _, c := range blocks {
  			if c.openStart > b.openStart && c.closeEnd < b.closeEnd {
  				violated = true // violation #8: nested DSML masked inside a parameter value
  				s, e := c.openStart-b.openEnd, c.closeEnd-b.openEnd
  				body = body[:s] + strings.Repeat(" ", e-s) + body[e:]
  			}
  		}
  		inv := DSMLCall{Name: dsmlBlockName(text[b.openStart:b.openEnd]), Args: map[string]any{}}
  		for _, pm := range dsmlParamRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(body, -1) {
  			key := pm[1]
  			if pm[2] == "" {
  				violated = true // violation #7: parameter missing the string attribute
  			}
  			if key == "justification" {
  				violated = true // violation #1: decorative justification parameter
  			}
  			val := decodeDSMLValue(pm[3], pm[2] == "true")
  			// Repeated parameters mean an array (DeepSeek models emit
  			// <parameter name="justification"> twice for a []string arg).
  			if prev, ok := inv.Args[key]; ok {
  				if arr, isArr := prev.([]any); isArr {
  					inv.Args[key] = append(arr, val)
  				} else {
  					inv.Args[key] = []any{prev, val}
  				}
  			} else {
  				inv.Args[key] = val
  			}
  		}
  		calls = append(calls, inv)
  	}
  	return calls, violated, nil
  }
  </｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  </｜｜DSML｜｜invoke>
  </｜｜DSML｜｜tool_calls>
